first.rationale: Prioritize onboarding simplification because both onboarding completion and activation are declining, and prior evidence links reduced friction to activation and time-to-value. Verify the direct onboarding evidence and the pricing evidence because competitor pressure makes pricing consequential, but acquisition lift alone may not establish sustainable qualified-revenue value after discounts and retention effects.

mid.rationale: Run onboarding simplification. It directly addresses the 4% completion decline and the 6% activation decline, while verified evidence shows materially higher completion (+13%), faster time-to-value (-2.1 days), and improved 30-day retention (+3%), supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not use promotional pricing: although it increased qualified revenue initially, the discounted cohort failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Monitor activation, qualified conversion, retention, and account quality as guardrails.

final2.rationale: Maintain onboarding simplification as the response. The deeper competitor cut and doubled price-related churn make pricing pressure urgent, but the verified discount experiment produced poor renewal survival, so broad discounting risks sacrificing sustainable qualified revenue for transient signups. Simplification is the best-supported available intervention for current completion and activation declines and has verified retention benefit. Track price-sensitive SMB churn and renewal outcomes as explicit guardrails; the evidence does not establish that onboarding alone offsets competitor-driven churn.
